text:
The University of Chicago was incorporated in 1857, succeeding the Old University of Chicago which closed in 1886. The new institution, established in 1890, began classes in 1892 under William Rainey Harper, who established the Divinity School as the first graduate professional school in 1891. The university operates on a quarter system.
Academically, the University of Chicago is organized into a college, four divisions of graduate research, seven professional schools, and the Graham School of Continuing Liberal and Professional Studies. It is known for its liberal arts undergraduate program, which features the Socratic method and a core curriculum. The university has made significant contributions to scientific thought, notably being the site of the Chicago Pile-1 (the first controlled nuclear chain reaction), Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment, and the development of the Chicago school of economics.
